senses.gloss:
gati
(‘movement’)
------------------------------------------
This word, though commonly it means ‘movement,’ is used in several other senses like consequence, path, nature, progress and so on.
The उपनिषद्स् and the Bhagavadgītā describe two types of gatis or paths (leading to a destination)—the śukla (the white, also called ‘arcirādimārga’) for the fortunate souls and the कृष्ण (the black, also called ‘dhūmādimārga’) for the ordinary ones.
Some of the पुराणस् predicate four gatis (or results) for human beings as follows: reaching the presence of a deity through यज्ञ, intense spirit of renunci-ation through तपस् or austerity, status of ब्राह्मण through कर्मसṁन्यास or renunciation of desire-motivated actions and कैवल्य or मोक्ष (liberation) through ज्ञान (spiritual wisdom).
In the Matsyapurāṇa गति is described as one of the eight daughters of कर्दम प्रजापति. She was married to the sage Pulaha. Her three sons once offended शिव and were cursed by him to die by drowning in the ब्रह्मपुत्र.
